introduction.text: The Domus di Amore e Psiche is a late‑antique Roman house in Ostia, notable for its elaborate interior decoration and the discovery of a small statue group of Amor and Psyche, which gives the building its name.

history.description: The Domus was built upon a 2nd‑century commercial building that had previously housed taverns.
Construction of the Domus in the second quarter of the 4th century AD on a pre‑existing 2nd‑century building.
The house is named after a small statue group of Amor and Psyche found in one of the cubicoli.

design.description: The entrance opens onto a vestibule with a side door leading to a central room with a mosaic floor and a private latrine.
Three small cubicoli feature white and black geometric mosaics, with one having painted walls and an opus sectile floor.
A small internal garden with a ninfeo, a podium with niches, and a marble water channel.
A two‑story representation room with opus sectile flooring and marble walls, including a fountain niche.

art.description: A small marble group depicting Amor and Psyche, the central artistic element of the house.
Geometric mosaics in the vestibule and cubicoli, including opus sectile.
Marble columns and marble lunense used in the garden and interior.
